spec.description: 1 means Alloy or Prometheus scraped the target. Target is 1 for every job. Red at 0. A red job is not being scraped, so its other panels go empty. Check that the process is healthy and that Alloy has a scrape block for it.
spec.title: Scrape targets (up)

spec.description: 95th percentile of snapshot time minus the source updated_at, per source. The source variable applies. Yellow at 30 seconds is the HR contract. Red at 300 seconds is the sales, product, and engineering contract. A red source is past every contract. Check that connector's last success and its logs.
spec.title: Snapshot lag p95 by source (s)

spec.description: Seconds since the last sync that advanced the watermark, per source. A cursor watermark leaves the series unset. Yellow at 30 seconds. Red at 300 seconds. HR polls every 10 seconds. The other sources poll every 60 seconds. Red means the connector has not completed a cycle inside the slowest contract.
spec.title: Last successful sync age (s)

spec.description: Snapshots written or skipped per second, per source. A skip means version, ACL, and hash already matched. There is no red threshold: a high rate is work, not a failure. If writes stay at zero while the source is changing, read snapshot errors.
spec.title: Snapshot writes and skips (/s)

spec.description: Snapshot failures per second by source and stage. Target is zero. Red above zero. contract means the object carried an excluded field. enqueue means the publish failed after the snapshot write. Read the connector logs for that source.
spec.title: Snapshot errors by stage (/s)

spec.description: Absolute difference between snapshot count and source count, per source. Target is zero. Red at one object. Negative drift is the same failure as positive drift. A red source is missing a snapshot or still has a deleted one. Run is not required: the next sync reconciles, unless delete verification is also red.
spec.title: Snapshot drift (objects)

spec.description: Same failures as the SLO stat, split by source and store, over the selected range. Target is zero. Red at one. s3 is the connector. postgres and neo4j are the worker. Do not ignore a red store: the object is still there after a delete.
spec.title: Delete verification failures in range (count)

spec.description: Logs from every connector. There is no color threshold. Use this when a source panel is red. The line names the object type, version, and byte count. It does not contain the body.
spec.title: Connector logs

spec.description: 1 after the connector or the ingestion worker loaded its contracts. Target is 1. Red at 0. A red worker has not finished startup. Read that service's logs. This stays 1 while the process waits on Postgres or the bucket.
spec.title: Workers (up)

spec.description: Error lines, and lines whose decision is deny. The service variable filters both. There is no color threshold. A deny is demo step 2: open the line and follow request_id. An error line is a failed sync, enqueue, or store write. The line has no snippet and no secret.
spec.title: Errors and denies

spec.description: 1 when Postgres, Neo4j, S3, or SQS answered the ingestion worker. Target is 1. Red at 0. A red dependency means the worker cannot finish a message. Check that store or floci, then the worker logs.
spec.title: Worker dependencies (up)

spec.description: Event lag is now minus occurred_at when the worker finishes the message. Watermark lag is one series per source. A cursor watermark is omitted. Yellow at 30 seconds is the HR contract. Red at 300 seconds is the other contracts. This is not oldest-message age. A red source is late: check queue depth and the worker logs.
spec.title: Ingest lag by source (s)

spec.description: Visible messages on kbs-p0, kbs-p1, and kbs-p2, from GetQueueAttributes. There is no red threshold: a short queue during a sync is normal. A depth that climbs and does not fall means the worker is not keeping up. Check workers and store errors.
spec.title: Queue depth (messages)

spec.description: Visible messages on each tier dead-letter queue right now. Target is empty. Red at one message on any queue. This is a gauge. Read the ingestion logs for the failing object, fix the cause, then replay.
spec.title: Dead-letter depth by queue (messages)

spec.description: Embedding calls per second by model, and skips per second by source. A skip is an unchanged content hash. The graph write still runs. There is no red threshold. A sudden jump in calls is a real content change, not by itself a failure.
spec.title: Embed calls and skips (/s)

spec.description: Absolute difference between indexed objects and the source object count, per source. Target is zero. Red at one object. Sits beside snapshot drift. A red source is in the bucket but not in the index, or the reverse. Check store errors and the worker logs.
spec.title: Index drift (objects)

spec.description: 95th percentile of one Postgres or Neo4j write, by store and operation. There is no red threshold in this POC. A line that climbs while store errors are red means that store is the bottleneck. Postgres is authoritative. Neo4j is the derived index.
spec.title: Store write latency p95 (s)

spec.description: Failed Postgres or Neo4j writes over the selected range, by store and operation. Target is zero. Red at one. The raw counter is the total since process start, so this panel uses increase. A red store left the message unacknowledged. Read the ingestion logs.
spec.title: Store errors in range (count)

spec.description: Logs from the ingestion worker. There is no color threshold. event_type and decision are in the line. request_id is in the line, not a label. Use this when queue depth, store errors, or dead-letter depth is red.
spec.title: Ingestion logs

spec.description: 95th percentile of search, get_document, and find_related. The surface variable applies. Target for search is under 0.25 seconds. Red at 0.25. Search includes the HR ACL re-check. A red search with a calm ACL re-check is the index. A red search with a slow re-check is the HR harness.
spec.title: Retrieval latency p95 by tool (s)

spec.description: Searches with no chunk, divided by all searches, by permission group. The permission group variable applies. There is no red threshold: an empty result is often a deny or a question with no overlap, and hash-v1 only returns a chunk that also matched full text. A group stuck at 100 percent is the access check. Compare with the deny log.
spec.title: Empty-result rate by group

spec.description: Rejected bearer tokens over five minutes, by reason. There is no red threshold: a demo that omits the token produces missing. A climb in invalid or expired means a bad or old token. clearance and missing_claim are a principal the gateway refused. secret means the process has no signing secret.
spec.title: Auth failures (count)

spec.description: Product notices over the selected range. ok, invalid, and error are separate. Target is no invalid and no error. Those two turn red at one. ok stays green. invalid means the body was refused. error means SQS did not take the notice. Read the webhook receiver logs.
spec.title: Webhook notices in range (count)

spec.description: Visible messages right now. The main hook queue can hold work, so it stays green. The dead-letter queue turns red at one message. A red dead-letter queue means a notice was not consumed. Read the product connector logs.
spec.title: Hook queue depth (messages)

spec.description: Finished requests per second by process and route. /health and /metrics are left out so scrapes do not hide traffic. An unknown path is the route unmatched. There is no red threshold. A rate of unmatched means clients are calling paths the process did not register.
spec.title: HTTP request rate (/s)

spec.description: Responses at 500 and above, per second, by process, route, and status. Target is zero. Red above zero. A red route is a failed request, not an auth denial. Auth denials are 401 and are on the auth panel. Read that service's logs.
spec.title: HTTP 5xx rate (/s)

spec.description: 95th percentile of request duration by process and route, in seconds. Health and metrics are left out. There is no red threshold here. The 0.25 second target is the search panel, not every route. Use this to see which route is slow.
spec.title: HTTP duration p95 (s)

spec.description: HR snapshot time minus the source updated_at, 95th percentile. Target is under 30 seconds, the HR contract. Red at 30. No samples means the connector wrote nothing in the window, so check the connector logs before treating it as a breach. This panel stays on HR when the source variable changes.
spec.title: HR snapshot lag p95 (s)

spec.description: 95th percentile of search, including the HR ACL re-check. Target is under 0.25 seconds. Red at 0.25. The surface variable applies. No samples means nobody searched. Open the retrieval panel to see which tool is slow.
spec.title: Search latency p95 (s)

spec.description: Visible messages across the tier dead-letter queues right now. Target is empty. Red at one message. This is a gauge. A red value means a message exhausted retries. Read the ingestion logs, then replay with make dlq-replay only after the cause is fixed.
spec.title: Dead-letter depth (messages)

spec.description: Deletes that still found the object, counted over the selected range. Target is zero. Red at one. The source variable applies. Check the store label: s3 is the connector, postgres and neo4j are the worker. A red value means a delete was not verified.
spec.title: Delete verification failures (count)

spec.name: source_id
spec.label: Source
spec.description: Limit source series to one department. All keeps every source.

spec.name: surface
spec.label: Surface
spec.description: REST or MCP. All keeps both.

spec.name: permission_group
spec.label: Permission group
spec.description: Highest-privilege group on the empty-result rate. All keeps every group.

spec.name: service
spec.label: Service
spec.description: Filters the error and deny log panel. All keeps every service. The value is .+ because Loki rejects an empty-matching .*.
